papers.title: Intrinsic neural timescales in autism spectrum disorder and schizophrenia. A replication and direct comparison study
papers.feature: Faced with results that only partly matched what they'd hoped to confirm, the authors repeatedly held their claims back — flagging that the brain-behavior links 'did not survive' their stricter statistical correction, calling weakly-supported findings something to treat 'cautiously,' and refusing 'more decisive conclusions' until larger samples are tested. A concrete look at calibrating one's claims to exactly what the evidence supports.

papers.title: Adult-Generated Hippocampal Neurons Allow the Flexible Use of Spatially Precise Learning Strategies
papers.feature: Rather than declaring victory, the authors actively raised the competing explanation that their drug might have dulled general mental abilities, ran extra checks (blood counts, motor and exploration tests) to argue against it, and still conceded the alternative 'cannot be completely ruled out' and that key links 'need to be clarified in further studies' — a concrete look at interpreting a striking result with restraint.

papers.title: Comprehensive Brain Tumour Characterisation with VERDICT-MRI: Evaluation of Cellular and Vascular Measures Validated by Histology
papers.feature: With only 21 patients and biopsies available for just a few of them, the team consistently sized their claims to that evidence: they call the work preliminary and exploratory, report trends that did not reach significance as exactly that, and explicitly state the sample 'does not allow generalisations' rather than declaring their tumour-distinguishing markers proven.

papers.title: Blinded Versus Unblinded Evaluations of Motor Scores in Patients with Parkinson's Disease Randomized to Deep Brain Stimulation or Best Medical Therapy
papers.feature: Despite finding that blinded and unblinded raters mostly agreed — a result that could tempt a sweeping claim that blinding is unnecessary — the authors deliberately held back, noting their small sample and other limitations and stating the question 'will require more research.' A clean example of letting a striking finding stand without overselling it.

papers.title: A systematic review of the incidence of schizophrenia: the distribution of rates and the influence of sex, urbanicity, migrant status and methodology
papers.feature: Faced with a finding (regional differences in schizophrenia rates) that could easily have been trumpeted, the authors deliberately hold back: they devote a whole 'Caveats' section to explaining that a review of other studies cannot prove a hypothesis but only suggest ones to test later, note that most of their own filtering rules were ad hoc and invite others to re-analyze, and explicitly endorse the warning not to interpret 'beyond the limits of the data.' A concrete look at conclusions kept proportional to the evidence.

papers.title: The effectiveness of Schroth method in Cobb angle, quality of life and trunk rotation angle in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.feature: Even though their pooled analysis found a statistically significant benefit, the authors refused to call it meaningful: they flagged that the spine-curve improvement fell short of the smallest change a patient would actually notice, rated their own evidence as low or very low, and listed the small samples and short follow-up that could inflate the numbers.

papers.title: Epigenetic-based age acceleration in a representative sample of older Americans: Associations with aging-related morbidity and mortality
papers.feature: Despite working with a fashionable biomarker, the authors deliberately temper their conclusions: they show their epigenetic aging measures predict health and death less well than cheaper, simpler facts like education and smoking, and they lay out a long list of caveats about where their tools might not transfer to other populations. A concrete example of resisting the pull to oversell a headline result.

papers.title: Recruitment of a Diverse Community-based Older Adult Cohort for a Longitudinal Aging Study
papers.feature: Rather than claim their growing enrollment proved their methods worked, the authors repeatedly held back: they note they raised the cash payment over time but 'cannot determine whether the payment increase led to the increase in participation,' and that they 'cannot say' how much the pandemic slowed things — keeping each conclusion to exactly what their data could support.

papers.title: Prevalence of rearrangements in the 22q11.2 region and population-based risk of neuropsychiatric and developmental disorders in a Danish population: a case-cohort study
papers.feature: When the data didn't support a firm claim, the researchers said so plainly — flagging that their young, modest-sized sample left them unable to settle the link with schizophrenia, and devoting a full section to where their numbers could mislead (e.g. carriers being more likely to come to medical attention in the first place). A concrete example of conclusions trimmed to fit what the evidence actually supports.

papers.title: ChatGPT applications in medical, dental, pharmacy, and public health education: A descriptive study highlighting the advantages and limitations

papers.title: The characteristics and extent of food industry involvement in peer-reviewed research articles from 10 leading nutrition-related journals in 2018

papers.title: Compositional data analysis enables statistical rigor in comparative glycomics

papers.title: MaNGA galaxy properties – II. A detailed comparison of observed and simulated spiral galaxy scaling relations
papers.feature: Throughout, the authors openly flag the limits of their own conclusions: they note their samples are statistically incomplete and 'caution is advised' when interpreting the data-model mismatch, state plainly that their findings hold only for massive disk galaxies, and admit they did not correct for certain blurring and non-circular-motion effects — a concrete example of fencing one's own claims with explicit qualifications.

papers.title: Study Protocol for the Fukushima Health Management Survey
papers.feature: Right in their own summary the authors flag the weakness that undermines their effort: barely one in five residents returned the basic questionnaire, which they call a 'critical problem' that 'complicates the estimation of health effects' — they attach the limitation to their own findings rather than letting it pass unmentioned.

papers.title: The stepped wedge trial design: a systematic review
papers.feature: In drawing conclusions from only 12 studies, the authors openly flag what could undercut them — noting their small sample 'makes generalisations difficult' and devoting a limitation to the real chance their search missed eligible studies, including a whole category of two-step trials.

papers.title: Measuring the crowd within again: a pre-registered replication study
papers.feature: When the authors ran extra analyses they hadn't planned in advance, they explicitly flagged them as exploratory and warned readers not to over-trust them — noting they had set no target sample size for those tests and hadn't specified the comparison beforehand. papers.title: The citation advantage of linking publications to research data
papers.feature: In its discussion the team lays out a candid list of its own constraints: it used only a free, partial slice of the literature, looked only at the formal data statements (possibly missing others tucked elsewhere), never checked whether the linked repositories actually held usable data, and leaned on a small sample of citations — each caveat fencing how far its citation-advantage claim should be read.

papers.title: CVEfixes: automated collection of vulnerabilities and their fixes from open-source software

papers.title: FAIR Data Reuse in Traumatic Brain Injury: Exploring Inflammation and Age as Moderators of Recovery in the TRACK-TBI Pilot

papers.title: Large-scale replication study reveals a limit on probabilistic prediction in language comprehension
papers.feature: After reporting a failed replication, the authors deliberately rein in their own conclusion: they explicitly flag that their negative result does not rule out the effect, that a quirk of their test design (the a/an article only signals the very next word) could explain the null finding, and that conclusions from single lab sentences may not carry to natural reading. A concrete look at researchers spelling out the ways their own headline claim could be wrong.

papers.title: Does stress consistently favor habits over goal-directed behaviors? Data from two preregistered exact replication studies
papers.feature: Reporting two failed replications, the authors openly qualify their own null result rather than overstate it: they note their food-satiation step may not have singled out one outcome as intended, that even the comparison group failed to show the expected behavior (so the key test was 'inadequate'), and that pandemic-era recruitment and a highly selective participant filter limit how far the conclusions reach.

papers.title: Intrinsic neural timescales in autism spectrum disorder and schizophrenia. A replication and direct comparison study
papers.feature: The authors repeatedly attach explicit cautions to their own findings: they flag that several promising results did not survive a stricter statistical correction, warn that small and age-imbalanced samples limit confidence, and write that their tentative brain-symptom links 'should be taken cautiously' and need replication in larger samples before firmer conclusions.

papers.title: Sensitivity analysis in multiple imputation in effectiveness studies of psychotherapy

papers.title: Exercise for osteoarthritis of the knee

papers.title: Neurosurgeons’ experiences of conducting and disseminating clinical research in low-income and middle-income countries: a reflexive thematic analysis

papers.title: Using positionality and reflexivity to support equity in partnership‐driven research

papers.title: The “7 Up” Intersectionality Life Grid: A Tool for Reflexive Practice

papers.title: Preliminary Evaluation of the Engagement and Effectiveness of a Mental Health Chatbot

papers.title: Caring for the caregivers: Evaluation of the effect of an eight-week pilot mindful self-compassion (MSC) training program on nurses’ compassion fatigue and resilience

papers.title: Helmets for preventing injury in motorcycle riders

papers.title: Blinded Versus Unblinded Evaluations of Motor Scores in Patients with Parkinson's Disease Randomized to Deep Brain Stimulation or Best Medical Therapy
papers.feature: After reporting that blinded and unblinded scores largely agreed, the authors plainly list what could undermine their own claim — too few surgery patients, scoring from video rather than in person, and two body-function items that video couldn't capture — and refuse to overstate, saying whether blinding can be dropped 'will require more research.'

papers.title: Short-term safety outcomes of mastectomy and immediate implant-based breast reconstruction with and without mesh (iBRA): a multicentre, prospective cohort study
papers.feature: The authors deliberately ran no formal significance tests, refused to draw causal conclusions from their non-randomized data, and repeatedly stamped their risk-factor findings as 'exploratory' and merely 'apparent' associations — a clear look at researchers fencing in their own claims rather than overselling them.

papers.title: Lactobacillus johnsonii N6.2 Modulates the Host Immune Responses: A Double-Blind, Randomized Trial in Healthy Adults
papers.feature: Rather than overstating its hopeful results, the team flags many of its findings as non-significant trends, notes that a key effect appeared only in one subgroup and 'will require confirmation,' and frames the whole effort as a small pilot whose benefits 'may take longer than 8 weeks to be quantified' — a study that openly hedges its own claims.

papers.title: Prevention of infections and fever to improve outcome in older patients with acute stroke (PRECIOUS): a randomised, open, phase III, multifactorial, clinical trial with blinded outcome assessment

papers.title: Integrated versus nonintegrated peripheral intravenous catheter in hospitalized adults (OPTIMUM): A randomized controlled trial

papers.title: What do we know about community-based health worker programs? A systematic review of existing reviews on community health workers

papers.title: A systematic review of the incidence of schizophrenia: the distribution of rates and the influence of sex, urbanicity, migrant status and methodology
papers.feature: The authors built an explicit 'Caveats' section that names the limits of their own work — that a review of the literature can't prove anything about the disease itself, that their study-selection rules were improvised, that they likely missed papers, and that the rates probably undercount true cases — and they repeatedly flag where their numbers should be read cautiously.

papers.title: Clinical effectiveness of Invisalign® orthodontic treatment: a systematic review
papers.feature: The reviewers openly attach warning labels to their own bottom line: because the underlying studies were too dissimilar to combine, they refuse to issue clear treatment recommendations and explicitly tell readers to interpret their findings 'with caution.' papers.title: Global Estimate of Human Brucellosis Incidence
papers.feature: The authors repeatedly flag the limits of their own estimate: they call it deliberately 'conservative,' state plainly that they left out misdiagnosis and underdiagnosis because the data were too thin (and that including those would push the number much higher), and concede the true figure 'remains elusive' — a clear look at researchers fencing their conclusion with stated qualifications.

papers.title: The effectiveness of Schroth method in Cobb angle, quality of life and trunk rotation angle in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.feature: Even though their analysis found the exercise method significantly reduced spinal curvature, the authors openly flag that the size of that reduction fell below the threshold patients would actually notice — and they rate their own pooled evidence as low to very low quality. A clear look at researchers tempering their own headline result.

papers.title: An integrative review of the effects of high-intensity interval training on the autonomic nervous system
papers.feature: Rather than overselling its upbeat headline, the review devotes a long stretch to undercutting its own conclusions — flagging that the studies used wildly different exercise protocols, were mostly men, had small samples and short follow-ups, leaned on an indirect heart measure, and likely suffered publication bias toward positive results — and explicitly says its findings are 'tempered' by these issues. A clear look at attaching honest qualifiers to one's own claims.

papers.title: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors as an alternative treatment in canine mast cell tumor
papers.feature: This review repeatedly tempers its own conclusions: even in its summary it warns that the pooled data lacked standardized samples and that this 'should temper the interpretation of the results,' and its discussion flags sponsorship bias, the missing comparison group, and the weak mutation-detection methods before stating TKIs still shouldn't be a first-line choice without stronger evidence — a clear look at attaching qualifications to one's own findings.

papers.title: Epigenetic-based age acceleration in a representative sample of older Americans: Associations with aging-related morbidity and mortality
papers.feature: The authors devote a full passage to flagging the limits of their own findings — admitting their clocks assume relationships hold across populations they never tested (e.g. a measure trained only up to age 45 being stretched to older adults), that their noise-correction method may not transfer to other samples, and that their results still need replication. A concrete look at qualifying one's own conclusions out loud.

papers.title: Recruitment of a Diverse Community-based Older Adult Cohort for a Longitudinal Aging Study

papers.title: Screening for loneliness in representative population samples: Validation of a single-item measure
papers.feature: When their own data showed the brief loneliness question matched the established scale only moderately, the authors said so plainly — labeling it 'weak convergent validity' right in the summary — and devoted a section to conceding what they couldn't establish (no validated cut-off, no diagnostic-accuracy check, limited generalizability), urging readers to interpret the results 'with caution.'

papers.title: MEG and EEG data analysis with MNE-Python

bridges.rationale: Caveating one's own limitations and documenting one's procedures are two distinct acts of voluntarily surfacing information the reader needs, bridging Honest and Transparent under a single quality of proactive disclosure.
Caveating one's claims and disclosing hidden facts are distinct acts, but both instantiate a single proactive willingness to volunteer information one could withhold, bridging Honest and Transparent.

Disclosing one's interests and reflexively naming one's standpoint are two aspects of voluntarily surfacing the author's own shaping influences, so naming it leads you to expect research that exposes its own situation rather than posing as neutral.

Non-selective (withholding no results) and Shared (withholding no materials) are two aspects of one higher quality of proactively volunteering everything rather than holding back, which predicts instances that disclose both inconvenient findings and underlying data.

Disclosing facts (like conflicts) and sharing materials (like data and code) are distinct aspects of a single readiness to make one's research contents available to others, and expecting that readiness predicts both behaviors.

Disclosing what could be hidden and refusing to cherry-pick what to report are distinct ways of volunteering rather than withholding information, bridging Transparent and Honest under a shared quality of withholding nothing.

Both proactively put potentially compromising information on the public record in advance — conflicts in one case, analysis plans in the other — binding future conduct, so naming the shared self-exposing commitment changes what you'd expect of the instances.

Both name a voluntary offering of withheld-able information — awkward ties under Honest, internal process records under Transparent — so a higher quality of proactively surrendering the optional-to-conceal bridges the regions and predicts over-sharing beyond the required minimum.
